date.as_written: Saṃmbat 839 kāttika (Verso 32:3) kṛṣṇa , paṃcami puṣva nakṣetre subha joge, ādityavāra

notes: The scribe's name, 'Jayarūndrasiṃha', is probably a corrupt spelling of Jayarudrasiṃha. The catalogue gives a chronogram: durggā(9) aginī(3) vasu(8). Read right to left this gives 839, which matches the colophon's Saṃbat 839, so NS 839 = 1718 CE (kārttika). The catalogue also gives a bracketed second date, 'saṃvat 831', with the same month, pakṣa, tithi, nakṣatra, yoga and weekday. This conflicts with 839. It may come from a second colophon or be a misreading; 831 would be 1710/11 CE. The quoted colophon does not name the king (Mahīndrasiṃha) or the place (Kathmandu); they appear only in the catalogue fields, so they are not listed as persons or place. The date fits the reign of Mahīndrasiṃha (Mahīndra Siṃha Malla) of Kathmandu, c. 1714–1722.
